idiom_name: ordered Express middleware stack mounted before the route handlers
implementation_notes: Node has no base-action class to extend, so the shared security sequence becomes a stack of middleware functions registered with app.use or router.use before the routes; each function runs its check and either answers (401/403) or calls next(). The stack is composed once per router, so every route declared after it inherits the processing, and the business handler is a plain callback containing no security code. Middleware is a framework feature, but the pattern's structure - one entry path applying shared checks - is preserved by mounting discipline rather than by inheritance.
code_sketch:
const security = [authenticate, authorize, validateSession];

router.use(security, audit);            // every route below passes through
router.get('/orders/:id', (req, res) =>
  res.json(orders.get(req.params.id)));  // business handler
pitfalls: A route registered before the security middleware never passes through it; mount the stack first and assert coverage in tests.
Forgetting to call next() or failing to end the response on rejection leaves the request hanging until the client times out.
A rejection path must return before the handler runs; calling next() after writing an error response lets the business code execute anyway.
